reconstruction.product_guess: Neon Warden, a browser-based vertical slice of a comedic/narrative top-down space shoot-'em-up.
reconstruction.how_to_get_it: Play it in a web browser with no install at adamsmith.systems (associated with course/project CM121 f26).
reconstruction.question_raised: Are the players actually the bad guys working for a greedy authority while the 'monsters' are just trying to protect their grown scouts and keep lanes open?
uncertain: What 'CM121 f26' refers to (likely a university course code and Fall 2026 term).
How the scanning cone / 'Codex' mechanic works alongside shooting.

scores.evidence: 00:00 opens immediately on active top-down shooter gameplay with bullets and enemies; genre is unmistakable within 1 second and there are no front-loaded logos.
Every shot builds up the dread of 'The Warden' (00:01-00:12) before subverting it at 00:14 with a comedic voice and a narrative twist at 00:22 ('They want them OWNED!'). No filler.
Synth music ramps up from 00:00 to 00:13, cuts completely to silence for the comedic fakeout (00:13-00:19), drops back in hard on the title card at 00:20, and resolves cleanly at 00:29.

Narrator sits cleanly over a low-passed synth bassline (00:01-00:10), the music swells when speech stops (00:11-00:13), and The Warden speaks during total silence (00:14-00:19) and a ducked groove (00:22-00:25).

Burned-in captions with speaker labels ('Lane Authority Briefing' vs 'The Warden') and exclamation marks ('?!') convey the setup and punchline muted, though the vocal contrast is big part of the joke.
Captions at 00:01, 00:07, 00:14, 00:16, and 00:22 are large, high-contrast white text on a dark pill background, accurately timed to speech, and strictly 1-2 lines.

Shots are well-paced overall, though the static camera hold on The Warden talking at 00:14-00:19 (6 seconds) and the gameplay shot at 00:22-00:27 (5 seconds with sparse firing) feel slightly low-energy visually.

fixes.problem: Small unvoiced pop-up text on the left ('SCOUT CHANNEL: Fine. I wasn't using this hull anybody.') appears during voiced narration, competing for reading attention and containing a typo ('anybody' instead of 'anyway').
fixes.fix: Hide or disable the secondary left-side 'SCOUT CHANNEL' UI pop-ups during the trailer capture so the viewer focuses strictly on the main captions and action.

fixes.problem: After the high-energy title drop at 00:20, the boss fight shot from 00:22 to 00:27 has very little bullet-hell action on screen—the boss doesn't fire back at all.
fixes.fix: Swap 00:22-00:27 for a capture where The Warden is actively firing dense neon bullet patterns while delivering the line, matching the intensity of the music drop.

fixes.problem: On silent autoplay, the visual contrast between the terrifying reputation and the whiny voice at 00:14 relies solely on punctuation in the caption.
fixes.fix: Add a subtle comedic visual cue or animation to The Warden (e.g., an angry shake/bounce synced to 'STOP! Stop right there!') to sell the tonal shift even when muted.

overall.summary: An exceptionally well-crafted 30-second trailer that nails the cold open, uses sound design and a music fakeout textbook-perfectly to land a comedic/narrative twist, and ends with a crystal-clear call to action; only minor visual lulls in the back half hold it back.
